sections.html:
Lafayette County's seat, Oxford, lies in north Mississippi some 75 miles south-southeast of Memphis, and the University of Mississippi (Ole Miss) is the center of town life. Sellers here usually deal with two offices: the city for permits and codes, and the county for property tax. The 2020 census population was 25,416. Highway 6, which also carries U.S. 278, runs west to Batesville and east to Pontotoc. Highway 7 runs north to Holly Springs and south to Water Valley, and Highway 30 heads northeast toward New Albany.

The terrain is the North Central Hills: forested ridges and red clay. Downtown rests on one ridge and the campus on another, with the main commercial corridors in the valleys between. If your lot slopes and sits on red clay, walk it after rain and check drainage and grading before listing.

sections.h2: How Ole Miss shapes the housing market
sections.html:
Nothing moves Oxford housing like the university, which is why the numbers here do not resemble the rest of north Mississippi. Enrollment hit 28,960 across all campuses in fall 2026, up 2 percent for a fourth straight record, and the 5,363 first-time freshmen made the third largest class ever. That pull keeps rentals and investor-owned houses a notable share of the market.

Student-market measureOxford, 2020 census
Median age27.8 years
Households11,856
One-person households43.8%
Housing units15,944 (25.6% vacant)
Homeowner vacancy rate2.9%
Rental vacancy rate19.7%

Only 19.8 percent of households include children under 18. Both vacancy figures are high for a city this size, so a landlord should compare lease end dates with the target closing date before choosing a sale route.

  • Owner-occupants selling a family home usually follow a normal listing path.
  • Landlords with student tenants should review lease end dates before setting a closing date.
  • Heirs of a house that needs work may prefer a quick as-is sale.

Oxford publishes Historic Design Guidelines for its older areas. Owners of houses in historic areas should read them before making exterior changes, and should tell a buyer about any approvals that were granted. The campus itself, called University, Mississippi, is unincorporated territory that the city of Oxford surrounds completely, so it is worth confirming which side of a boundary your address falls on when a question about services comes up.

The Building division administers the building, electrical, mechanical, plumbing and fuel gas codes and the erosion control ordinances. It accepts residential and commercial permit applications, performs inspections and issues certificates of occupancy or completion. Permit applications and inspection scheduling are moving to an online system called EnerGov.

The adopted codes are the 2024 International Building Code, the 2024 International Residential Code with local changes, the 2023 National Electrical Code, plus 2024 plumbing, mechanical, fuel gas and fire codes. Fee schedules, including a 2026 permit fee chart, are public.

Renovated without a permit? Expect the buyer's inspector to ask for the file. On a hilly lot, read the erosion control ordinance, since grading and clearing can trigger requirements. Some cash buyers will take a house with permit questions still open, though you should disclose what you know. Details are on the City of Oxford Building and Development page, and all ordinances are on Municode.

sections.h2: Lafayette County property tax and homestead
sections.html:
Lafayette County bills the tax, due by February 1 each year. Payment can be made at the office, by phone or online, with a 2.35 percent fee on cards. The state counts an owner's own single-family home at 10 percent of true value and every other kind of real property at 15 percent, which makes a rental pay on a bigger slice of its value.

Real property gets revalued at least every four years. Owners who disagree can ask the Board of Supervisors for a hearing, usually by the first Monday in August. Inside Oxford, county, school district and city rates all apply. Whoever owns the house of record on the January 1 assessment date gets the bill, and the closing agent usually divides the year between you and the buyer.

Apply for homestead exemption with the tax assessor from January 1 through April 1. New ownership or a change in who lives there can require a fresh application, as when a student-area house turns from rental to owner-occupied. A tax sale is where unpaid taxes can end up, so pay them or arrange a payoff before closing.

Oxford has two public school districts. Most addresses are in the Oxford School District, and a few outlying sections belong to the Lafayette County School District, so verify yours because families ask early. The city also runs a bus service, Oxford-University Transit, and students and faculty ride free with university identification.

sections.h2: Timing a sale around the academic year
sections.html:
Oxford's calendar runs on the university's. A landlord who closes while tenants are still in place hands the buyer the lease, and a buyer who wants a vacant house will wait for the lease to end. Owners of a family home face no such constraint, though listing near campus draws more attention when students, parents and faculty are in town. Decide early whether you want the house shown occupied or empty, and set your closing target to match.

Whatever route you take, a title search comes first. It lists liens and unpaid taxes, the balance is paid from your proceeds, and the deed is signed at closing. Gather permit records, repair receipts and lease copies beforehand, and bring photo identification and any mortgage payoff figure to the closing.

sections.h2: Your options for selling in Oxford
sections.html:
An agent listing, a private sale and a cash offer are all open to you. With a market shaped by the university, the right choice depends on who owns the house and how it looks. A renovated home near campus may draw interest through a listing, while an inherited house with deferred repairs may fit a cash sale better.

The written property condition disclosure statement has to reach the buyer before title transfers (Mississippi Code section 89-1-503). Late delivery gives the buyer a cancellation right: three days after in-person delivery, five after mailing.

We buy houses in Oxford as is, with no commission and no closing costs to you. Give us the address and we will walk through how a cash offer works and what timeline fits. Turn it down and you owe nothing.

Rentals sell as is to cash buyers fairly often. Look at lease end dates and the tenants' rights before you pick a closing date, and give the buyer the leases and rent records. A student house that sits empty between terms still costs taxes, insurance and utilities, so a sale timed to a lease end can save money.

faqs.q: How far is Oxford, MS from Memphis?
faqs.a: About 75 miles south-southeast of Memphis, Tennessee. Highway 6 and Highway 7 are the main routes into the city.

faqs.q: How many students attend Ole Miss?
faqs.a: The University of Mississippi reported 28,960 students across all campuses in fall 2026, a 2 percent increase and its fourth straight enrollment record.

faqs.q: When are Lafayette County property taxes due?
faqs.a: February 1 each year. The tax collector's office takes payment in person, by phone or online, and charges a 2.35 percent fee on cards.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for renovations in Oxford, MS?
faqs.a: The Building division issues residential and commercial permits and performs inspections. Contact the city to confirm whether your project needs one.

faqs.q: Can I sell a student rental in Oxford for cash?
faqs.a: Yes. Cash buyers often purchase rentals as is. Check your lease end dates and the tenants' rights before choosing a closing date.
